key_insight: A factory–processor interface separates verified, code-dependent optical resource preparation from reusable Gaussian processing for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
engineering_relevance: With advance resource preparation and sufficient routing parallelism, deeper error-correcting codes increase parallel resource width without lengthening the protected online sequences of the demonstrated constructions.
method: Prepare verified logical Bell resources offline using recursively concatenated C4 codes built from physical GKP qubits.
Inject resources into a time-domain measurement-based processor through an interface tracking mode mappings, measurements, frames, and verification records.
Construct logical CNOT, Bell measurement, SWAP, and Hadamard operations with address and code-permutation tracking.
evidence_signal: Simulations at 12.25 dB support decreasing logical Bell errors from concatenation levels 2 through 5; a separate fixed-sample evaluation at 15.6 dB and level 2 gives one-sided 95% binomial upper bounds below 10⁻⁵, both with and without prescribed post-injection noise.
watch_item: The reported gains depend on the specified displacement-noise model and fixed postselection policy; practical scaling also requires sufficient routing parallelism and advance resource availability.
paper_title: Modular optical fault-tolerant quantum computation via an interface between verified resources and online logical operations
